spec_gaps.description: INV-POOL-3's own text scopes the guarantee to 'a JDT LS process exits for any reason' (any exit cause), but the invariant's own observable-seam column and this prove-feature's context note both narrow the concrete test mechanism to 'kill the child mid-request' / 'kill the real child process' -- an abrupt, crash-like death. Not treated as an ambiguity requiring two readings: the design's own worked example for this invariant is the kill scenario, and a graceful/clean-exit variant (exit code 0 with no in-flight requests, or a deliberate shutdown) is not what feat-prove-pool-crash-handling's falsifier describes ('a request in flight when the child process dies hangs...'). This plan covers the kill-mid-request instance the observable seam names; it does not add a separate condition for a graceful-exit-while-busy variant, to avoid inventing scope beyond what this feature's falsifier and the invariant's own seam column commit to.
spec_gaps.location: docs/design/runtime-model.md#INV-POOL-3 (invariant text vs observable-seam column); feature_list.json#feat-prove-pool-crash-handling (falsifier, context)

spec_gaps.description: The 'deadline' INV-POOL-3's observable seam measures against is the per-call deadline from X-001, which cross-cutting.md marks 'open' (recommended default 30s, not yet finalized). Not treated as a blocking ambiguity: feat-prove-readiness's own context note already resolves the analogous case by instructing the test to parameterize the deadline rather than hard-code 30s, and this plan's conditions follow that same precedent so they do not depend on X-001 being settled.
